name: Iperion Limited
overview: Iperion Limited is a pre-revenue NZX-listed micro-cap (market cap ~NZ$1.5m) whose sole asset of substance is an exclusive worldwide licence to Pathoglaze, a self-cleaning antimicrobial surface coating originally developed for applications such as furniture, egg cartons, chopping boards, textiles, automotive plastics and hospital curtains, with current development effort concentrated on Pathoglaze-infused polymer jute bags for shipping cocoa and coffee beans. The company has never recorded a dollar of sales revenue since acquiring the licence and is now sustained only by a related-party loan facility and the goodwill of its 77%-controlling shareholder. It is the corporate shell of what was, until circa 2021-2022, Southern Charter Financial Group Limited, a cash-box company with no operating business that was searching for an acquisition; that predecessor entity has no bearing on Iperion's current prospects.

business_model.summary: Iperion holds an exclusive worldwide licence to manufacture, use, sell, distribute, import and export Pathoglaze, an antimicrobial surface coating, and is attempting to convert product trials with large multinational manufacturers (most prominently an unnamed multinational chocolate manufacturer, for cocoa/coffee shipping bags) into long-term commercial supply agreements. There is currently NO revenue-generating business — the company is entirely pre-commercial. Manufacturing/production would be outsourced to a third-party operator, Three Summit Ventures, under a Pilot Outsourcing Agreement with a normally fixed $400,000/year facility fee, which the operator has voluntarily and fully waived for FY2025, FY2026, FY2027 and FY2028 given the absence of production volume. The licence's own contractual customer-number and revenue performance targets (SGD$150,000 of sales by September 2026) were permanently waived by the inventor subsequent to the FY2026 year end, along with the royalty owed to the inventor — evidence that even the counterparties closest to the technology no longer expect near-term commercial traction on the original timeline.

revenue_streams.name: Product sales (Pathoglaze)
revenue_streams.trend: none — zero revenue since inception of the licence

business_model.customer_type: Intended B2B / large multinational manufacturers (chocolate, food packaging, textiles, automotive) who would need to incorporate Pathoglaze into their own manufacturing processes — implies long, uncertain sales-conversion cycles and no current customer base
business_model.geographic_mix: NZX-listed holding company (New Zealand); licensed technology and outsourced pilot manufacturing based in Malaysia (Three Summit Ventures); controlling shareholder and lender base in Malaysia/Hong Kong

main_competitors: Established antimicrobial coating suppliers (e.g., BioCote, Sanitized AG, Microban International)
Silver-ion and copper-based antimicrobial additive producers
In-house antimicrobial R&D of large packaging/textile/automotive manufacturers
Alternative shipping/packaging preservation technologies for cocoa and coffee (e.g., modified-atmosphere packaging, fumigation, conventional jute treatments)
competitive_position.market_position: Effectively pre-market — Iperion has no disclosed market share, no signed commercial customers, and no independently verifiable competitive standing; it is a technology licensee attempting to prove out a niche application (antimicrobial shipping bags) rather than an established supplier

moat_factors.description: Legal exclusivity to Pathoglaze provides a nominal barrier to direct replication of this specific formulation, but the underlying antimicrobial-coating technology space is well populated by established competitors with proven commercial products, and exclusivity has produced zero sales in the years the licence has been held

An unnamed multinational is trialling Pathoglaze-infused jute bags, but this is a development/trial relationship, not a signed supply contract, and the customer relies on Iperion incorporating the coating into its own manufacturing chain — a long, non-guaranteed conversion path
No established brand presence in target end-markets

weaknesses: Zero revenue in every year since the licence was acquired; no proof of commercial viability

Total dependence on a single outsourced manufacturing partner (Three Summit Ventures) that has repeatedly waived its own fixed fees rather than being paid, indicating the pilot facility is itself uneconomic at current volumes
No independent balance-sheet capacity — company relies entirely on a related-party facility from the controlling shareholder to remain solvent
Original licence performance targets (customer numbers, SGD$150,000 revenue by Sept 2026) were permanently waived rather than met, removing the only externally set commercial milestone

Extreme shareholder concentration (77.4% held by one individual) means public shareholders have essentially no influence and the stock has almost no free float or liquidity to exit a deteriorating position

growth_drivers: Conversion of the cocoa/coffee shipping-bag trial with a multinational chocolate manufacturer into a signed long-term supply agreement — the single most important near-term catalyst

Expansion of Pathoglaze into other previously trialled applications (furniture and egg carton coatings, chopping boards, odour-combating textiles, automotive plastics, food containers, hospital curtain coatings) if any commercial traction is achieved
Research grants secured by the outsourced manufacturing operator (Three Summit Ventures) that are subsidising ongoing product development at no direct cost to Iperion
Potential drawdown of the Elitesoft Asia facility (expandable to US$1,000,000 subject to shareholder and NZX approval) to fund a scale-up if a commercial order materialises

Cost discipline: directors have deferred 50% of fees and 33% of the management fee, and the outsourcing partner has waived its fixed fee through to March 2028, extending the company's cash runway independent of sales

business.description: The company has never sold Pathoglaze commercially; all disclosed 'progress' consists of trials, not contracts, after several years of trying

All production capability sits with one outsourced operator (Three Summit Ventures) in Malaysia; Iperion can terminate the Pilot Outsourcing Agreement at any time with no break fee, but has no independent manufacturing fallback

The original commercial milestones under the Pathoglaze licence (customer numbers and SGD$150,000 revenue by Sept 2026) were permanently waived post year-end rather than achieved, and the inventor's royalty was also waived — both signal the technology has not commercialised on the timeline originally contracted
Target customers must integrate Pathoglaze into their own manufacturing processes, a slow and non-guaranteed path with no visibility on timing

financial.description: Auditor issued a Material Uncertainty Related to Going Concern paragraph; cash of $155,492 against an annual operating outflow of ~$269,849 implies well under 12 months of runway on cash alone, before accounting for the related-party facility

Solvency depends on the controlling shareholder's 12-month support letter and the Elitesoft Asia facility (from a company related to that same shareholder); if that support is withdrawn or the facility is not honoured, the company likely cannot continue as a going concern

financial.risk: Dilution / control risk from facility expansion
financial.description: The Elitesoft Asia facility is expandable to US$1,000,000 subject to shareholder/NZX approval; conversion or refinancing of debt this size at a $0.003 share price (market cap ~NZ$1.5m) would be enormously dilutive to the ~14% free float and could further entrench the controlling shareholder's already-dominant 77.4% stake
Total equity is just $53,803 against total assets of $184,251 and liabilities of $130,448 — a thin buffer that a single further loss-making year would likely erase

regulatory.description: A near-shell company with a market cap of ~NZ$1.5m, going-concern uncertainty and near-zero trading liquidity faces ongoing risk of NZX scrutiny, additional disclosure obligations, or in a worst case suspension/delisting if it cannot demonstrate a viable ongoing business

Expansion of the Elitesoft Asia facility to US$1,000,000 requires shareholder and NZX approval, given Elitesoft's relationship to the controlling shareholder/director Mr Chang Ku EE; execution risk exists around securing and structuring that approval fairly to minority holders

Any commercial rollout of an antimicrobial coating used in food packaging (cocoa/coffee bags) or hospital settings would require compliance with food-contact-safety and other jurisdiction-specific regulatory regimes, adding time and cost to commercialisation

macro.description: The stock shows zero trading volume in recent sessions despite an official 'Trading' status; the last apparent real trade was in October 2025, meaning holders may be unable to sell at any price even if they choose to exit

As a going-concern company with no revenue, Iperion's ability to raise any future equity capital (beyond the related-party facility) is highly sensitive to general risk appetite for speculative micro-caps

macro_factors.industry_outlook: The broader antimicrobial coatings and specialty surface-treatment industry has genuine secular demand drivers (food safety, hygiene standards, post-pandemic antimicrobial awareness), but that industry-level tailwind is largely irrelevant to Iperion specifically until it can demonstrate it has captured any commercial share of it — the company's fate depends on company-specific execution (a signed customer), not the macro trend
macro_factors.cyclicality: Not meaningfully cyclical in the traditional sense — the business has no revenue base to be cyclical; risk is binary (commercialisation success vs. failure/wind-down) rather than tied to an economic cycle
macro_factors.interest_rate_sensitivity: Direct and material — the company's primary funding lifeline (the Elitesoft Asia facility) is priced at 8% (Hong Kong Monetary Authority Base Rate + 4%), so the cost of its only meaningful funding source moves with HKMA rates
key_input_costs: Outsourced manufacturing/plant fees (currently fully waived through FY2028)
Coating raw material inputs (undisclosed, borne by the outsourced manufacturer)
Professional/listing/audit costs of maintaining an NZX listing

recent_developments.event: FY2026 annual report released: net loss narrowed to $294,595 (FY2025: $455,683), aided almost entirely by the manufacturing partner fully waiving its $400,000/year fixed fee; cash fell to $155,492 (from $425,341) and total equity to $53,803; auditor issued a Material Uncertainty Related to Going Concern paragraph

Licence performance targets (customer numbers and SGD$150,000 revenue by Sept 2026) and the inventor's royalty were permanently waived — removing the only externally contracted commercial milestone for the Pathoglaze licence

Three Summit Ventures (outsourced manufacturing operator) agreed to fully discount its $400,000/year fixed fee for a further two years through to 31 March 2028, extending the cash-preservation runway independent of sales

Company entered a new $250,000 loan facility with Elitesoft Asia Sdn Bhd (a company related to majority shareholder/director Mr Chang Ku EE) at 8% interest (HKMA Base Rate + 4%), expandable to US$1,000,000 subject to shareholder and NZX approval; this replaces the earlier interest-free NZ$150,000 loan Mr EE provided on 15 June 2026
Mr Chang Ku EE (77.4% shareholder) confirmed a 12-month financial support commitment from the date of approval of the FY2026 financial statements
Directors agreed to defer 50% of directors' fees and 33% of the management fee from January 2026 until sufficient sales are achieved, to conserve cash
H1 FY2026 (unaudited) interim results released: net loss narrowed to $158,254 (H1 FY2025: $363,730) as the manufacturing plant fee discount began; cash of $241,882 at 30 September 2025
Last apparent genuine trade in IPR.NZ shares occurred around this time; the stock has since shown essentially zero trading volume despite retaining an official 'Trading' status on NZX

No public evidence was found of any material announcement after 30 June 2026 (the FY2026 annual report date) as of this analysis (12 August 2026) — no first commercial sale, no confirmed outcome of a shareholder vote on expanding the Elitesoft facility to US$1,000,000, and no delisting or suspension notice

items.target: No formal target disclosed; base case forecast assumes NO sales
items.notes: Management's own base-case going-concern forecast is built on zero sales activity, underscoring that no near-term commercial revenue is assumed even by the company itself
Three Summit Ventures has agreed to fully discount the $400,000/year fixed fee for both remaining years to March 2028

items.target: Sufficient to cover costs for the next 12 months, based on the approved base case with no sales and utilising the Elitesoft loan facility
items.notes: Explicitly conditional on the loan facility and the majority shareholder's support commitment being honoured; auditor still flagged material uncertainty

items.target: Up to US$1,000,000, from the current $250,000 Elitesoft Asia facility
items.period: Subject to shareholder and NZX approval, timing undisclosed
items.notes: No confirmed date found for the shareholder vote; availability is also contingent on the related-party lender continuing to honour its commitment

guidance.management_commentary: Directors describe the year's improved (smaller) loss as driven almost entirely by fee waivers from the outsourced manufacturing partner rather than any operating improvement, and reiterate the company is still 'working toward securing long term sales agreements' with no committed timeline. There is no revenue guidance beyond an explicit zero-sales base case.

bull_case: A single signed long-term supply agreement with the multinational chocolate manufacturer for Pathoglaze-infused cocoa/coffee shipping bags could transform the company from a going-concern shell into a revenue-generating licensor almost overnight, given the tiny current market cap (~NZ$1.5m)
Committed related-party support (Elitesoft Asia facility plus Mr Chang Ku EE's 12-month funding letter) removes near-term insolvency risk, buying time for a commercial breakthrough

Cost base has been aggressively stripped back — manufacturing fees waived through March 2028, director/management fees partly deferred — meaning even modest future sales would flow through to a much-improved loss position

Option-like risk/reward: at a ~NZ$1.5m market cap, the downside per share is small in absolute dollar terms while a successful commercialisation of a novel antimicrobial technology across multiple addressable end-markets (packaging, textiles, automotive, healthcare) offers a large theoretical multiple

The controlling shareholder has both the means and a demonstrated willingness (multiple waived fees, loans, support letters) to keep the company alive, reducing (but not eliminating) near-term liquidation risk
bear_case: Pre-revenue for the entire life of the Pathoglaze licence with no committed customer contract — years of trials have not converted to a single sale, and the original licence's own revenue/customer targets were permanently waived rather than met

Going concern is explicitly flagged by the auditor; cash of $155,492 against an annual burn of ~$269,849 means the company would be insolvent within months without related-party support that is not guaranteed to continue

Governance and dilution risk are unusually acute: the controlling shareholder (77.4%) is also, via a related company, the company's primary lender, and any conversion/expansion of that facility to US$1,000,000 at a $0.003 share price would be massively dilutive to the ~14% free float with little minority protection given the shareholder's existing control

Effectively zero liquidity — the stock shows no real trading volume since around October 2025 despite an official 'Trading' tag, meaning existing holders may be unable to exit at any price, and the market cap (~29x book equity, ~10x cash) reflects option value rather than a price discovered through actual trading

Market capitalisation (~NZ$1.5m) already prices in speculative optionality on a commercial breakthrough that management's own base-case forecast assumes will NOT happen in the next 12 months; if the trial with the chocolate manufacturer fails to convert, or the related-party funding is withdrawn, equity value could go to approximately zero
